newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London unchanged, await Tankan.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London unchanged, await Tankan.

text.p: Japanese shares in London were barely changed on Tuesday as investors were cautious ahead of Wednesday's Tankan report on corporate sentiment, traders said.
The Nikkei/ISE 50 index was up 1.14 points at 1,606.68 points.

Earlier in Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 tumbled after the Dow Jones had marked its second biggest daily decline, triggered by remarks of Japanese Prime Minister Hashimoto Monday evening that Japan could sell U.S. Treasuries. The index closed 94.21 points, or 0.46 percent, lower at 20,341.93 points.
The impact of Hashimoto's remarks was softened on Tuesday as officials repeatedly reassured Japan was not about to dispose T-bonds.
"We did a little better than Tokyo", one trader said. "But investors are now focusing the Tankan report", one trader said.
The Tankan report, due Wednesday morning, reviewing corporate sentiment, would give the market new direction, dealers said.
Shares in carmakers were the most actively traded issues, traders said. Honda Corp. was up 85 yen at 3,365 yen, compared with a close of 3,330 yen in Tokyo.
Earlier today, May car output figures showed that Honda increased its production by 29 percent.
Toyota was up 20 yen to 3,375 yen, while Nissan gained 8.50 yen to 816.50 yen.
Toyota and Nissan raised their output by 8.2. respectively 18 percent in May.
